Alex — thanks for the clear list and the spreadsheet. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Kim (ops) so we can give concise, auditable answers. I’ll summarize what I can right away and highlight the items we need Ops/legal to confirm:

1) Pinning scope (quick answer): For hosted Redwood API customers we offer region pinning at the account-level. That pin governs primary inference processing and persistent storage (model caches are considered ephemeral unless customer turns on long-term workspace persistence). Backups/snapshots: by default backups are stored in the same region; we can commit to US-only backups in the DPA addendum on a per-account basis (requires a brief provisioning window).

2) Transient egress window (quick answer): Our default failover window is 72 hours for cross-region reroute for availability, but for high-availability customers we offer shorter SLAs and can constrain failover to a 24-hour transient window via policy. Telemetry: while a transient egress window is active we retain delivery logs, region routing events, and minimal redaction-safe request telemetry for 30 days (longer retention is configurable with Ops/legal agreement).

3) Subprocessors & KMS: We maintain a region-specific subprocessor roster. I can attach the latest roster snapshot and the network topology for your review. For keys: if you use Redwood-managed KMS we can provide the HSM/KMS region (e.g., us-east-1) and support split-key escrow on request. For customers with strict residency we recommend customer-managed KMS in their VPC.

Attachments: network-topology.png (image/png)

Marissa / Kim — please confirm the wording we can add to the DPA addendum (I’ve also drafted a short addendum and attached it as a docx). Alex — apologies if any of the above is more detail than you need; happy to jump on a 30m to walk through specifics.

Alex — thanks for the questions and the spreadsheet. I reviewed Logan’s summary and provided proposed DPA addendum language below that addresses the three items. High level: we can commit to region-locational pinning for primary processing and backups where customers purchase the Residency Addendum. Temporary cross-region processing will be limited, logged, and subject to notification/consent as follows.

Proposed snippets for the addendum (draft):
• Residency Scope: "Redwood will ensure that Customer data subject to the Residency Addendum shall be processed and stored in the designated geographic region (United States). Redwood shall not transfer or process such data outside the designated region except in the limited circumstances outlined in this Addendum."
• Backups and Snapshots: "Backups, snapshots, and persistent data copies created by Redwood will be stored in the designated region. Temporary relocation for operational purposes may be used subject to the transient egress rules below and will be limited to the minimum time necessary."
• Transient Egress & Notification: "Redwood may, as necessary for availability or incident remediation, temporarily process or route Customer data through an alternate geographic region for up to 72 hours (the ‘Transient Egress Window’). Redwood will log each such event, notify the Customer within 4 hours of initiation, and provide an event report within 48 hours. Customers may request a shorter Transient Egress Window (e.g., 24 hours) via their account configuration or as part of a dedicated SLA."
• Subprocessor & KMS Disclosure: "Redwood will provide a current roster of subprocessors for the designated region upon execution of this Addendum and will publish changes to the roster with 30 days’ notice. For customers using Redwood-managed KMS, Redwood will disclose the KMS region and supporting infrastructure. Customers requiring keys to remain in-customer-control will be supported via customer-managed KMS integrations."

Next steps: I’ll upload this addendum to DocuSign once we get a confirmation from Alex that the runtime behaviors described match their requirements. Kim — can you confirm the 72-hour default operational window and whether we have a 24-hour configurable option today? Also please attach the subprocessor CSV snapshot to the DocuSign package.
